items.statement: Anatomy & Physiology
Course Focus
items.notes: [Apply the following for each content standard.]

items.statement: Identify SDA Christian principles and values in correlation with science.
Recognize God’s power as Designer, Creator, Sustainer, and Redeemer in the universe.
Acknowledge God as the Author of all scientific principles and laws regardless of man’s interpretation.
Develop stewardship and service attitudes toward health, life, and earth’s environment.
Apply Biblical principles of Christian morality, integrity, and ethical behavior to all aspects of life.
Equip students with Christian perspectives on scientific issues.
Course Abilities
items.notes: [Apply the following to each content standard.]

items.statement: Develop abilities in science. HS-ETS1
Develop critical and creative thinking skills (analysis, evaluation, divergent questioning, modeling).
Understand and utilize the scientific method of problem solving.
Utilize the principles and methodologies of cooperative learning.
Be able to apply science knowledge and skills to a variety of purposes. HS-ETS1
Recognize scientific principles and laws as tools to solve problems in everyday life.
Apply the scientific method in analysis of controversial topics, e.g., cloning, global warming, stem cell research.
Read, write, and interpret scientific documents (lab write-ups, journals, scientific publications).
Conduct research in the content area.
Engage in various uses of technology.
COURSE CONTENT:Anatomical Orientation, Cells and Tissues, Systems
items.notes: [Understand, explore, analyze, apply.]

items.statement: Be able to understand principles of anatomy and physiology.
Recognize God as the designer and creator of the human body.
Define and properly use anatomical orientation terminology.
Demonstrate an understanding of the structure of cell types and tissues.
Identify the components within each system (skeletal, digestive, circulatory, etc.). HS-LS1-2
Describe the major chemical and cellular processes necessary for maintaining life (cellular respiration, protein synthesis, mitosis, meiosis). HS-LS1-1, 1-4, 1-6, 1-7, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3
Be able to safely explore human anatomy and physiology.
Examine anatomy of specimens.
Explore human cells and tissues with microscopes. HS-LS1-2
Investigate the function of components within each system. HS-LS1-2, 1-3, 1-7
Be able to analyze human physiology.
Interpret the relationship between the structure and the function of cell types and tissues. HS-LS1-2, 1-7, 3-1, 3-2
Evaluate the relationship between the structure and the function of organs. HS-LS1-3
Correlate the structure of each organ system with its function. HS-LS1-2
Analyze the interdependence of organ systems in the body. HS-LS1-2, 1-3
Be able to apply principles of anatomy and physiology to health and life.
Strengthen belief in God as Designer and Creator from studying anatomy and physiology. HS-LS1-3
Utilize the concepts of anatomy and physiology to improve lifestyle choices. HS-LS3-2
